items.title: Section: Fixed and Unfixed Lifespans Across the Four Continents — From a Thousand Years Without Exception to Ten Years in an Age of Weapons

items.zh: 除贍部洲人壽分量，所餘生處壽量決定。此贍部洲，或時壽命廣無有量，或時短促，壽量不定。北拘盧洲人壽量隨轉，如決定量畢竟隨轉，無中夭故。餘一切處名不隨轉。贍部洲人十歲時壽，名為少壽。傍生一分，亦名少壽。所以者何？一分傍生，或一日夜壽量可得；或有一分若二、若三，乃至極多十日十夜壽量可得。非想非非想處受生有情，名為多壽，經於八萬大劫數故。
items.en:
Second, explaining each; first, fixed and unfixed lifespans; first, lifespans that are fixed. Apart from the measure of a human lifespan in Jambudvīpa, every other place of rebirth has a fixed lifespan. Second, lifespans that are unfixed. In Jambudvīpa, lifespan is sometimes vast and immeasurable, sometimes brief — the lifespan here is unfixed.
Second, whether the course is followed or not; first, following the course. The people of Uttarakuru have a lifespan that follows its course, their fixed measure invariably followed through completely, with no premature death. Second, not following the course. Every other place is called not following the course.
Third, short and long lifespans; first, short lifespans; first, a portion of Jambudvīpa's people. A ten-year lifespan among the people of Jambudvīpa is called a short lifespan. Second, a portion of animals. A portion of animals likewise have a short lifespan. Second, long lifespans. Beings reborn in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception have a long lifespan, spanning a full eighty thousand great eons.

items.title: Section: Bounded and Unbounded Lifespans — the Arhat's Final Life Against the Ordinary Being's Endless Wandering

items.en: Fourth, bounded and unbounded lifespans; first, bounded lifespans; first, arhats and others. Arhats and those in a comparable state are said to have a bounded lifespan.

items.title: Section: The Life Faculty Completes — Bounded Lives, Unbounded Wandering, and the Boy the Fire Could Not Touch

items.zh: 若諸有學於現法中定般涅槃，若諸異生住最後有，亦名有邊際壽。當知所餘，壽無邊際。若阿羅漢等、若諸如來、若諸菩薩，於壽行中延促自在，所有命根，名自勢力轉。當知所餘，名非自勢力轉。復次，云何眾同分？
items.en:
Second, learners and others. Learners certain to attain final nirvāṇa within this present life, and ordinary beings dwelling in their final rebirth, are likewise said to have a bounded lifespan. Second, unbounded lifespan. One should know all remaining beings have an unbounded lifespan.
Fifth, determined or not determined by one's own controlling power; first, determined by one's own controlling power. Arhats, tathāgatas, and bodhisattvas alike have complete mastery over extending or shortening their own life faculty; this is called determined by one's own controlling power. Second, not determined by one's own controlling power. One should know all remaining beings are called not determined by their own controlling power.
Third, the class of sentient beings; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is the class of sentient beings?

items.title: Section: What Makes Beings "The Same Kind" — Six Ways of Sharing a Class, and Who Can Never Be Killed by Anyone at All

items.zh: 謂若略說，於彼彼處受生有情，同界，同趣，同生，同類、位、性、形等，由彼彼分互相似性，是名眾同分，亦名有情同分。此中或有，有情由界同分說名同分。謂同生一界。或有有情，由趣同分說名同分。謂同生一趣。或有有情，由生同分說名同分。謂同生一生。或有有情，由類同分說名同分。謂同一種類。或有有情，由分位、體性、容色、形貌、音聲、覆蔽、養命同分說名同分。
items.en:
Second, the explanation; first, stating its establishment. In brief, beings reborn in this or that place who share the same realm, destiny, generation, species, condition, nature, or form, are, through whatever portion of resemblance they share, called the class of sentient beings, also called the sameness shared among sentient beings.
Second, explaining each individually; first, sameness of realm. Some beings are called the same class through sameness of realm — that is, being reborn together in the same realm. Second, sameness of destiny. Some beings are called the same class through sameness of destiny — that is, being reborn together in the same destiny. Third, sameness of generation. Some beings are called the same class through sameness of generation — that is, being born together within the same generation.
Fourth, sameness of species. Some beings are called the same class through sameness of species — that is, belonging to the same kind. Fifth, sameness of condition and the rest. Some beings are called the same class through sameness of condition, nature, complexion, form, voice, shelter, and livelihood.

items.title: Section: Sameness Through Shared Merit or Fault, and What Makes an Ordinary Being an Ordinary Being

items.zh: 過失、功德同分說名同分。如殺生者望殺生者，廣說乃至諸邪見者望邪見者；離殺生者望離殺生者，乃至正見者望正見者；從預流者乃至阿羅漢、獨覺望預流等，菩薩望菩薩，如來望如來；如是更互說名同分。復次，云何異生性？謂三界見所斷法種子唯未永害量，名異生性。此復略有四種。一、無般涅槃法種性所攝，二、聲聞種性之所隨逐，三、獨覺種性之所隨逐，四、如來種性之所隨逐。
items.en:
Sixth, sameness through shared fault or merit; second, explaining it. Those who take life, in relation to others who take life, and so on in full up through those of wrong view in relation to others of wrong view; those who abstain from killing in relation to others who abstain, up through those of right view in relation to others of right view; from stream-enterers up through arhats and independently-awakened ones in relation to their own kind, bodhisattvas in relation to bodhisattvas, tathāgatas in relation to tathāgatas — in this way, reciprocally, this is called sameness of class.
Fourth, the state of being an ordinary being; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is the state of being an ordinary being? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. Within the three realms, so long as the seeds of phenomena eliminated by the path of vision have simply not yet been permanently destroyed, this is called the state of being an ordinary being.
Second, distinguishing its kinds. This is, in brief, of four kinds: first, those subsumed under no lineage capable of nirvāṇa; second, those accompanied by the śrāvaka lineage; third, those accompanied by the independently-awakened lineage; fourth, those accompanied by the tathāgata lineage.

items.title: Section: Association Begins — Six Kinds, From a Single Moment of Feeling to an Entire Future Rebirth

items.zh: 復次，云何和合？謂能生彼彼諸法諸因、諸緣，總略為一，說名和合。即此亦名同事因。又此差別者，或有領受和合，謂六處緣觸，或色等緣、或作意等緣，或觸緣受。或有引生後有和合，謂無明緣行等，受緣愛，愛緣取，廣說乃至生緣老死。或有六處住和合，謂四食及命根。
items.en:
Fifth, association; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is association? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. The totality of all causes and conditions capable of generating this or that phenomenon, taken together as one, is called association — this is also called the cooperative cause.
Second, distinguishing its kinds; first, association in receiving. There is furthermore association in receiving: the six sense-bases serve as condition for contact, or form and the rest serve as condition, or attention and the rest serve as condition, or contact serves as condition for feeling.
Second, association giving rise to a future existence. There is association giving rise to a future existence: ignorance conditions volitional formations, and so on, feeling conditions craving, craving conditions grasping, and so on in full up through birth conditioning ageing and death.
Third, association in the six sense-bases' abiding. There is association in the six sense-bases' abiding: the four kinds of nourishment together with the life faculty.

items.title: Section: Twelve Conditions for Purification, and the Six Points of Reverent Harmony That Let a Community Actually Function

items.zh: 或有工巧處成辦和合，謂工巧智及彼相應業具、士夫作用。或有清淨和合，謂十二種無雜集會，即自他圓滿等。又有世俗和合，謂諸有情依等意樂增上力故，互不相違，無諍無訟，亦不乖離。
items.en:
Fourth, association in accomplishing a skilled craft. There is association in accomplishing a skilled craft: craft-knowledge together with its corresponding tools and a person's own effort.
Fifth, association in purification. There is association in purification: the twelve unmixed convergent conditions, namely the perfection of self and other, and so on.
Sixth, association within ordinary worldly life. There is furthermore association within ordinary worldly life: sentient beings, through the force of a shared aspiration, remain mutually unopposed, free of dispute or litigation, and undivided from one another.

items.zh: 復次，云何名身？謂依諸法自性施設、自相施設。由遍分別，為隨言說，唯建立想，是謂名

items.title: Section: Phrase and Syllable Complete the Trio — And Why Nothing Named Is Ever Simply "Real" or "Unreal"

items.zh: 身。云何句身？謂即依彼自相施設、所有諸法差別施設，建立功德、過失、雜染、清淨、戲論，是謂句身。云何文身？謂名身、句身所依止性所有字身，是謂文身。
items.en:
Second, phrase-body. What is a phrase-body? Relying on that self-characteristic, the many distinctions among phenomena are established, setting forth merit, fault, defilement, purity, and conceptual proliferation — this is called a phrase-body.
Third, syllable-body. What is a syllable-body? The syllables underlying both name-bodies and phrase-bodies — this is called a syllable-body.

items.title: Section: What a Syllable, a Name, and a Phrase Can Each Convey — And the Five Branches of Learning Where Language Operates

items.zh: 又於一切所知所詮事中，極略相是文，若中是名，若廣是句。若唯依文，但可了達音韻而已，不能了達所有事義。若依止名，便能了達彼彼諸法自性、自相，亦能了達所有音韻，不能了達所簡擇法深廣差別。若依止句，當知一切皆能了達。又此名句文身，當知依五明處分別建立。所謂內明、因明、聲明、醫方明、世間工巧事業處明。
items.en:
Second, revealing their function; first, briefly stating it. With respect to all that is known and expressed, the very briefest characteristic is a syllable, the intermediate is a name, and the most extensive is a phrase.
Second, explaining each; first, syllable. Relying on a syllable alone, one can only make out sound and cadence, unable to grasp the meaning of any matter. Second, name. Relying on a name, one can grasp a phenomenon's own nature and characteristic, and can also make out sound and cadence, yet cannot grasp the deeper, broader distinctions of what is discerned. Third, phrase. Relying on a phrase, one should know that everything can be grasped.
Third, distinguishing where this operates. One should know that these bodies of name, phrase, and syllable are established, in their distinctions, within five branches of learning: namely, inner learning, logical reasoning, linguistics, medical science, and worldly craft and technical skill.

blocks.text: More "dissociated formations": lifespan, what makes beings the same kind, the coming together of conditions, and the units of language.
Apart from the humans of Jambudvīpa, every place of rebirth has a fixed lifespan. Master Cháng Bǎi: people of Uttarakuru live a thousand years, and none dies early.
Master Cháng Bǎi: arhats, buddhas, and bodhisattvas can extend or shorten life at will.
Beings who resemble one another in some part form a class. Master Cháng Bǎi: we are all monastics who live on alms, so we too are of one class.

Defined by the seeds eliminated on the path of seeing, as long as they are not destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi: though ordinary, each differs in the seeds within; some have uncontaminated seeds yet are undetermined among the three vehicles.
All the causes able to produce a thing, taken together, are its "association". Master Cháng Bǎi: to contact an object one needs the faculty, the object, and attention; then contact, then feeling.
Master Cháng Bǎi: practice needs this many conditions to come together; it is not as easy as one imagines.

The briefest is a syllable, the middle a name, the fullest a phrase. A syllable conveys only sound; a name conveys a thing's nature; a phrase conveys everything. (Untranslated, 0587c11: a "name" is set up on the nature and characteristics of things, through discrimination, to follow speech.)
"It is not as easy as one imagines." Twelve conditions must come together for practice to succeed. That is a reason for patience with oneself.

quiz.q: Where is lifespan unfixed, according to the treatise?
options: Uttarakuru
the heavens
Jambudvīpa
the animal realm
quiz.why: The treatise says that apart from the human lifespan of Jambudvīpa every other place of rebirth has a fixed lifespan; in Jambudvīpa it is sometimes vast and sometimes brief. Master Cháng Bǎi: people at the start of the eon could reach immeasurable years, then decrease to eighty thousand, then to thirty, twenty, and ten.

quiz.q: Whose lifespan "follows its course," and why?
options: the people of Jambudvīpa: their lifespan shifts with karma
the people of Uttarakuru: their fixed measure is followed through, with no premature death
beings in the peak sphere: it lasts eighty thousand great eons
arhats and the like: they extend or shorten it at will
quiz.why: The treatise says the people of Uttarakuru have a lifespan following its course, with no premature death, and every other place does not follow it. Master Cháng Bǎi: their lifespan is a thousand years, and all live to a thousand without dying midway.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain a "bounded" lifespan and "one's own controlling power"?
options: ordinary beings' short lives are bounded; the gods' long lives show controlling power
an arhat, entering final nirvāṇa after this life, has a bounded span; arhats, buddhas, and bodhisattvas extending or shortening life at will have controlling power
Uttarakuru's fixed thousand years are bounded; the peak sphere's eighty thousand great eons, long by one's own doing, show one's own controlling power
an arhat's mastery is the bounded span; an ordinary being's last existence shows controlling power
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: an arhat enters nirvāṇa without remainder when this life is over, so that lifespan is bounded. Arhats, buddhas, and bodhisattvas can live as long as they wish, with mastery in extending or shortening life, which the treatise calls determined by one's own controlling power.

quiz.q: What does the treatise mean by the class of sentient beings?
options: one real thing wholly identical in all beings
beings sharing realm, destiny, species, and so on, through whatever portion of resemblance they share
the gods reborn together in one heaven
members of a community under the same precepts
quiz.why: The treatise says that through whatever portion of resemblance beings share, this is called the class of sentient beings. Master Cháng Bǎi: because they have some parts in common and resemble one another, this is the class of beings. So it is resemblance in some portion, not a real thing wholly identical in all.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give for sameness of livelihood?
options: people of one hometown eating the same food
monastics all sustaining life on alms
merchants all living by trade
members of one family living together
quiz.why: The treatise lists sameness of condition, nature, complexion, form, voice, shelter, and livelihood. Master Cháng Bǎi gives his own example: we are all monastics who sustain life on alms, and so we too are of the same class.

quiz.q: Those who take life in relation to others who take life, and those of right view in relation to others of right view: what sameness is this?
options: sameness of destiny and of generation together
sameness of generation
sameness of condition
sameness through shared fault or merit
quiz.why: The treatise lists these under sameness through shared fault or merit, running from killers up through tathāgatas in relation to tathāgatas. Master Cháng Bǎi: they are called the same class because of having the same fault or the same merit.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define the state of being an ordinary being?
options: so long as the seeds of what is eliminated by cultivation have not been destroyed
wholesome roots severed, with no further good arising
so long as the seeds of what is eliminated by seeing, within the three realms, have not been permanently destroyed
not having received full ordination or joined the community
quiz.why: The treatise defines it by the seeds eliminated by the path of vision within the three realms, so long as they have not been permanently destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary beings in the three realms who have not wholly uprooted the afflictions eliminated on the path of seeing are all so called.

quiz.q: The English has "pursued by the śrāvaka lineage." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the four kinds of ordinary being, and what does 隨逐 convey?
options: four by wealth and rank; 隨逐 means being chased by karma
four by mode of birth; 隨逐 means continuing rebirth
though ordinary, beings differ in seed-tendency, some having undefiled seeds with vehicle undetermined; 隨逐 means a lineage accompanying one
all four are already noble; 隨逐 means following noble ones in training
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though ordinary beings, each differs in the seed-tendency within; some have uncontaminated seeds yet are undetermined among the three vehicles. The English "pursued by" sounds as though one were being chased, whereas 隨逐 means a lineage accompanying one.

quiz.q: What is association, and what is its other name?
options: each phenomenon's own seed; also called the generative cause
a gathering of the community; also called the observance day
mind and factors arising together in correspondence, all of them taken as one; also called the co-existent cause
all the causes and conditions able to generate a phenomenon, taken as one; also called the cooperative cause
quiz.why: The treatise says all the causes and conditions able to generate this or that phenomenon, taken together as one, are called association, also the cooperative cause. Master Cháng Bǎi gives the same reading.

quiz.q: How are the twelve unmixed convergent conditions of association in purification counted?
options: two perfections, of self and of other, each opened into five, so two plus ten makes twelve
the twelve links each purified in turn
the twelve sense-bases, inner and outer, free of defilement
hearing all twelve divisions of scripture
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: of the two perfections each has five, which opened out make ten; two and ten are twelve. He adds that practice needs this many conditions for pure convergence, and that it is not as easy as one imagines.

quiz.q: The English has "the six sense-bases take the six objects as condition" for 六處緣觸. According to the lecture, what is the structure of this sentence?
options: the six bases take the six objects as condition, and the objects take attention, each in turn
contact conditions the six bases and feeling conditions contact, the reverse order
the bases, objects, and attention directly cause feeling, without contact
the six bases, six objects, and attention are all conditions for contact, and contact conditions feeling; the six bases do not take the objects as condition
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi, following the Sub-commentary: to contact an object one needs the unimpaired eye and other faculties as condition, the objects present as condition, and attention rousing the mind as condition; only then is there contact, and after contact, feeling. So all of these condition contact. The English instead has the six bases take the six objects as condition.

quiz.q: What is the order of brevity among syllable, name, and phrase? Note that the English varies between "syllable" and "letters" for 文.
options: the briefest is a name, the intermediate a syllable, the most extensive a phrase
the briefest is a phrase, the intermediate a name, the most extensive a syllable
the briefest is a syllable, the intermediate a phrase, the most extensive a name
the briefest is a syllable, the intermediate a name, the most extensive a phrase
quiz.why: The treatise says the very briefest is a syllable, the intermediate a name, and the most extensive a phrase. Master Cháng Bǎi: the simplest is 文, expressed by a single character. The English uses "syllable" here and "letters" in the preceding section, so the one term 文 is not rendered consistently.

quiz.q: What can reliance on a name alone convey, and what can it not?
options: only sound and cadence, and not the meaning of any matter
a phenomenon's own nature, characteristic, and sound, but not the deeper, broader distinctions of what is discerned
everything, without exception
the deep and broad distinctions, but not sound and cadence
quiz.why: The treatise says a syllable gives only sound and cadence, a name gives own nature, characteristic, and sound, and a phrase gives everything. Master Cháng Bǎi: a name cannot reach deeper content or the deeper and broader distinctions of what is discerned.
